context_prefix_rationale: CSRP (CloSet RePaint). CLRP is already used by SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_INT_RP (ceiling RP). CSRP has zero collisions in the codebase — verified against id_registry.json context_prefixes_in_use and all spec production.json files.
scope_summary: Repaint of previously painted fixed closet shelving systems in residential homes. Covers shelf surfaces, cleats, and rods counted by opening tier (S/M/L/XL) per BuiltIns_Shelving Quantification System. This is the simplest RP spec — utility surfaces with lower quality expectations (QT2-QT3 only), brush-only application, and minimal protection. RP-specific additions: condition assessment (brief), degloss (if existing sheen warrants it), state-driven primer (adhesion or stain-block for mildew), and customer walkthrough. Does NOT cover closet walls (SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP), closet ceiling (SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_INT_RP), closet trim (SF_TRIM_INT_RP), closet doors (SF_DOOR_INT_RP), wire shelving (not paintable), or freestanding/removable shelving (not fixed).

relevant_findings.topic: Closets are utility-grade surfaces with reduced quality expectations
relevant_findings.finding: Closet interiors are not scrutinized surfaces. Occupants interact briefly (reaching for items), viewing distance is arm's length at best, and lighting is typically poor (single overhead bulb or none). QT4/QT5 are not justified for closet shelf paint — the labor premium for fine-finish prep/interstage is wasted on surfaces no one examines closely. NC spec supports QT2-QT5; RP spec restricts to QT2-QT3 only. QT2 = economy (1 finish coat, minimal prep), QT3 = standard (2 finish coats, thorough prep). Global QT modifiers apply: QT2 = 0.80, QT3 = 1.00.

relevant_findings.topic: Brush-only application — spray is not justified for closet shelving RP
relevant_findings.finding: NC closet shelving supports brush_roll, spray, and spray_rolloff. For RP, spray is not justified: closet shelving scope is typically small (2-10 openings per closet), spray containment in a closet is impractical (small enclosed space, contents typically nearby), and the surfaces are utility-grade where brush marks are acceptable. RP spec restricts to brush_roll only. This eliminates TSK_PRIME_SPRAY, TSK_PRIME_SPRAY_ROLLOFF, and TSK_FINISH_SPRAY from the task set.

relevant_findings.topic: Five interior RP substrate states apply, but closets predominantly see sound paint or mildew
relevant_findings.finding: Interior RP defines 5 substrate states: SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT, SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_INT_PEELING, SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE, SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE. For closet shelving, the two most common states are: (1) SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT — existing paint is sound, just needs refresh (most common); (2) SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE — closets in bathrooms, basements, or poorly ventilated spaces accumulate moisture and mildew on shelving. SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_INT_PEELING are less common on shelving than on walls/doors because shelving has less mechanical stress. SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE applies in smoking households. All 5 states are supported for completeness.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition assessment is brief for closet shelving
relevant_findings.finding: Unlike doors (which require adhesion testing, coating ID, moisture meter checks), closet shelving assessment is a simple visual scan: check for peeling, mildew, moisture staining, and general paint condition. No adhesion test needed (shelving has minimal mechanical stress — no hinges, no handling). No coating ID needed (closet shelves are almost always latex; oil-based paint on closet shelves is extremely rare). Moisture check is visual (look for mildew, water stains) rather than meter-based. Assessment is a single combined task, not split into multiple subtasks like doors.
relevant_findings.source: Interior_RP_Gap_Analysis.md Section D; Contrast with SF_DOOR_INT_RP_v1/research.json RF-004

relevant_findings.topic: Edge seal is NOT_APPLICABLE in RP — already sealed in NC or prior paint
relevant_findings.finding: NC closet shelving includes TSK_EDGE_SEAL for bare MDF edges to prevent fiber raise. In RP, all shelf edges are already sealed under existing paint coatings. Even if existing paint is failing, the MDF edge fibers are sealed by the original primer/sealer. Edge seal is NOT_APPLICABLE for RP. This is the only NOT_APPLICABLE task from the NC set.

relevant_findings.topic: Degloss may not be needed — closet shelves often have flat or eggshell finish
relevant_findings.finding: Closet shelving typically receives flat or eggshell sheen (utility surfaces). Unlike doors (semi-gloss/satin, requiring thorough degloss), closet shelves often have low-sheen existing finishes where degloss is minimal — light scuff sand with 150 grit is sufficient. Degloss is included as a task but at a faster rate than door/trim degloss. For closets with satin existing finish, more thorough degloss is needed. Chemical degloss is rarely used on closet shelves — mechanical scuff is standard.

relevant_findings.topic: Mildew treatment is the primary RP-specific concern for closet shelving
relevant_findings.finding: Closets are prone to mildew due to poor ventilation, especially in bathrooms, basements, and exterior wall closets. Mildew on shelf surfaces requires biocide treatment (bleach solution or commercial mildewcide) before painting. This is the most common RP-specific remediation task for closets. Stain-block primer (acrylic, not shellac — mildew stains are water-based) is required after biocide treatment to prevent stain bleed-through. Allow 24 hr dry time after biocide application before priming.

relevant_findings.topic: Contents removal is homeowner responsibility — no labor task
relevant_findings.finding: Closet contents (clothing, shoes, storage items) must be removed before painting. This is typically the homeowner's responsibility, communicated during project scoping. Unlike furniture moving in room RP (which painters may handle), closet contents are personal items that homeowners prefer to handle themselves. No labor task for contents removal. A brief pre-painting check that closet is cleared is absorbed into the assessment task.

relevant_findings.topic: Opening count quantification transfers unchanged from NC to RP
relevant_findings.finding: The opening count method (S/M/L/XL tiers per BuiltIns_Shelving Quantification System) transfers directly from NC to RP. Existing shelving has the same geometry as new shelving — opening dimensions do not change for repaint. Depth, detail, and access modifiers also transfer unchanged. The only modifier difference is QT range restriction (QT2-QT3 only for RP vs QT2-QT5 for NC).

relevant_findings.topic: Customer walkthrough is brief for closet work
relevant_findings.finding: RP customer walkthrough for closets is minimal — quick visual check that shelves are coated, no drips on floor/walls, and closet is ready for contents replacement. This is a fraction of the walkthrough time for doors or room-level work. Walkthrough is per-closet (EA_CLOSET), not per-opening.
relevant_findings.source: Interior_RP_Gap_Analysis.md Section C (RP_NEW additions); Professional practice

condition_drivers.effect: Mildew on closet shelving requires biocide treatment + stain-block primer. Most common remediation scenario for closets. Bathroom and basement closets are highest risk.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual inspection for mildew spots, musty odor, water staining.

condition_drivers.effect: Flat/eggshell existing finish = light scuff only. Satin existing finish = moderate degloss. Higher sheens are uncommon on closet shelving.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual assessment of existing sheen during condition scan.

condition_drivers.effect: Failing or peeling paint requires scrape/feather before recoating. Less common on shelving than on walls/doors but possible in moisture-damaged closets where paint delaminates from substrate.
condition_drivers.assessment_method: Visual scan for cracking, lifting, or delamination.

quality_differences.description: Economy closet shelf repaint — minimal prep, 1 finish coat. Appropriate for rental units, utility closets, pre-sale refresh.
quality_differences.inspection: Glance check — no drips, no misses, full coverage.

quality_differences.description: Standard closet shelf repaint — thorough prep, 2 finish coats. Appropriate for owner-occupied homes, visible closets.
quality_differences.inspection: Quick visual at arm's length. No drips, even coverage, clean edges.
quality_differences.sanding_between_coats: None — closet shelving does not warrant interstage sanding at QT3.

failure_modes.cause: Painting over mildew without killing spores first. Spores grow under paint film.
failure_modes.frequency: Common in bathroom/basement closets if not treated
failure_modes.prevention: Biocide treatment (bleach solution or mildewcide) before any coating. Allow 24 hr dry. Use stain-block primer.
failure_modes.remediation: Strip to substrate, treat with biocide, reprime, recoat.

failure_modes.cause: Water stains on shelving not sealed before topcoat. Tannin/mineral stains migrate through standard latex.
failure_modes.prevention: Stain-block primer (acrylic stain-blocker) over all stained areas before finish coat.
failure_modes.remediation: Apply stain-block primer over failed topcoat, then recoat.

failure_modes.failure: Adhesion failure on glossy existing finish
failure_modes.cause: Applying new coating over existing satin/semi-gloss finish without adequate degloss. New film cannot bond to smooth glossy surface.
failure_modes.frequency: Occasional — closet shelves are usually flat/eggshell
failure_modes.prevention: Scuff sand or chemical degloss before coating. 150 grit minimum.
failure_modes.remediation: Sand failed areas, degloss, reprime if needed, recoat.

notes_for_materials_manager.note: RP closet shelving needs only the standard acrylic enamel system (SYS_CLOSET_SHELF_STANDARD from NC). No premium waterborne urethane system needed — QT4/QT5 are excluded. Primer: acrylic stain-block for moisture damage states; standard acrylic primer for failing/peeling states. No primer needed for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (most common). No shellac needed — closet shelves rarely have smoke damage severe enough to warrant shellac (unlike doors).

notes_for_materials_manager.topic: Sheen restricted to flat and eggshell
notes_for_materials_manager.note: Closet shelving in RP uses flat or eggshell finish only. Satin is available in NC but unnecessary for RP utility surfaces. Flat is default (maximizes hide, minimizes prep demands). Eggshell for homeowners who want slight washability.

Include bleach solution or commercial mildewcide in consumables for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE scenarios. Usage rate: 1 application per closet (all surfaces treated together). Allow 24 hr dry before priming.

notes_for_sop_librarian.note: Closet shelf RP has the simplest module structure of all 9 RP specs: (1) Assessment — brief visual scan per closet, (2) Setup — floor protection, (3) Prep — degloss/scuff + spot fill + caulk repair + scrape/feather if needed + mildew treat if needed, (4) Prime — state-driven primer (conditional), (5) Finish — brush/roll finish coats, (6) Cleanup — protection teardown + brief walkthrough. No interstage module — QT2/QT3 do not require interstage sanding for closet shelving.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Assessment is a single combined task
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: Unlike doors (4 separate assessment tasks), closet shelving assessment is one task: visual condition scan. No adhesion test, no coating ID, no moisture meter. Quick scan for peeling, mildew, water stains, general condition. Assign substrate state. 2-3 minutes per closet.

notes_for_sop_librarian.topic: Prep tasks carry forward from NC with RP modifications
notes_for_sop_librarian.note: NC prep tasks (dust_wipe, light_sand, spot_fill, caulk) transfer with modifications: (1) dust_wipe becomes degloss/scuff — same action but different purpose (adhesion profile vs dust removal); (2) light_sand is absorbed into degloss; (3) spot_fill transfers DIRECT (fill nail holes, minor defects); (4) caulk becomes caulk_repair — assess existing caulk and replace failed sections only (not full re-caulk like NC).

notes_for_estimation_engineer.topic: Opening count UOM unchanged from NC
notes_for_estimation_engineer.note: RP uses identical UOM structure: EA_OPENING by tier S/M/L/XL for opening-based tasks, EA_CLOSET for per-closet tasks (protection, walkthrough). PS keys: PS_OPENING_EA.CLOSET_SHELF.S/M/L/XL for openings, PS_PROTECT_SF.FLOOR_WORKZONE for floor protection. No new PS keys needed.

Depth (SHALLOW 1.0, DEEP 1.15, VERY_DEEP 1.30), detail (SIMPLE_BOX 1.0, FACE_FRAME 1.20, CROWN_VALANCE 1.35, BEADED_ROUTED 1.50), and access (OPEN_ACCESS 1.0, CRAMPED 1.25, OBSTRUCTED 1.50) modifiers from NC production.json transfer unchanged to RP. Max stack: 1.30 x 1.50 x 1.50 = 2.93x — under 4.0x flag threshold.
Per Interior_RP_Gap_Analysis: 7 DIRECT + 6 MODIFIED - 1 NOT_APPLICABLE + 3 RP_NEW = ~15 tasks. This is the lowest task count of all 9 interior RP specs, reflecting closet simplicity.

Key gate patterns: (1) TSK_CSRP_ASSESS — always (all RP work); (2) TSK_CSRP_DEGLOSS — always (rate varies by existing sheen); (3) TSK_CSRP_SCRAPE_FEATHER — SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_INT_PEELING only; (4) TSK_CSRP_TREAT_MILDEW — SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE only; (5) TSK_CSRP_PRIME_STAIN_BLOCK — SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE, SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE; (6) TSK_CSRP_PRIME_ADHESION — SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT, SS_INT_PEELING; (7) No primer — SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (most common).
NC includes TSK_INTERSTAGE_SAND for QT4/QT5. Since RP closet spec is QT2-QT3 only, interstage sanding is eliminated entirely. This removes 1 task from NC set.

assumptions.source: Collision analysis against id_registry.json and all spec files
assumptions.note: CLRP is used by ceiling RP. CSRP has zero existing usage. Verified no TSK_CSRP_* IDs in codebase.

No doctrine explicitly prohibits QT4/QT5 for closet shelving. Restriction based on practical judgment that fine-finish prep is not justified for closet interiors. Reviewer may override to include QT4 if homeowner demand exists.

assumptions.source: Professional practice — small confined space argument
assumptions.note: NC supports 3 methods. RP restriction based on impracticality of spray in occupied-home closets with small scope. Reviewer may override for production scenarios (10+ closets in vacant home).

assumptions.value: Homeowner removes closet contents; no labor task included
assumptions.note: Standard industry practice is homeowner-handled. If contractor must handle contents, it would be a separate scope line item, not part of this spec.

assumptions.value: No interstage sanding for QT2-QT3 closet shelving
assumptions.source: Quality_Tiers_and_Surface_Condition.md — interstage is QT4+ for non-fine-finish surfaces
assumptions.note: Interstage sanding at QT3 is for fine-finish surfaces (doors, trim). Closet shelves are not fine-finish. NC spec confirms TSK_INTERSTAGE_SAND applies_when QT4/QT5 only.

uncertainties.description: NC allows flat, eggshell, and satin for closet shelves. RP research restricts to flat and eggshell. Some homeowners may request satin for closet shelves in walk-in closets or pantries where shelves are more visible. Should satin be included?
uncertainties.impact: Minor — satin does not change task set, only material selection and degloss rate for future RP work on these surfaces.
uncertainties.resolution: Materials Manager to decide. Recommend including satin as an option for completeness.

zones.notes: Drop cloth under closet opening. Identical to NC. RP always has finished floors. ~2-3 min setup per closet.

protection_zones_analysis.notes: Closet shelving RP has the minimal protection footprint — one zone (floor_workzone) only. No wall masking (brush_roll only, no overspray), no hardware (shelves have no hardware), no adjacent surface masking (shelf-to-wall junction is caulked gap, not a spray edge). This matches NC exactly.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Shelf back meets closet wall. Gap caulked during prep. No cut-in at paint time. Brush_roll on shelves does not create overspray risk for walls. Identical to NC adjacency.

affected_conditions.notes: RP is always in existing homes — floor_type defaults to finished. Floor protection always required.
Active moisture = STOP condition. Source must be resolved before painting. Bathroom/basement closets are highest risk. Moisture check is visual (no meter for shelving).

valid_input_states.rationale: Interior closet shelf RP operates on previously painted surfaces. All 5 interior RP states supported. Does NOT accept SS_BARE, SS_PRIMED_*, or NC states — bare/uncoated substrates are NC scope. Most common state is SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (simple refresh). Second most common is SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE (bathroom/basement closets).

output_state.rationale: Output state varies by selected sheen. Eggshell is default for closet shelving RP (slight washability for utility surface).

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: Brush_roll application on shelving creates no overspray risk for adjacent walls regardless of wall state. Shelf-to-wall gap is caulked. No masking needed.

required_paintscope_keys.purpose: Small openings count (6-18" x 6-18"). Drives per-opening tasks.
Medium openings count (18-36" x 12-30"). Drives per-opening tasks.
Large openings count (36-60" x 18-42"). Drives per-opening tasks.
XL openings count (60"+ x 30"+). Drives per-opening tasks.
Depth modifier: SHALLOW / DEEP / VERY_DEEP. Drives rate modifier.
Detail modifier: SIMPLE_BOX / FACE_FRAME / CROWN_VALANCE / BEADED_ROUTED. Drives rate modifier.
Access modifier: OPEN_ACCESS / CRAMPED / OBSTRUCTED. Drives rate modifier.
Floor protection area under closet opening.
Surface condition (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) for prep modifier. GOOD = sound paint, FAIR = localized failure/mildew, POOR = widespread failure.

not_applicable_tasks.reason: Bare MDF only — edges already sealed under existing paint in RP. No exposed MDF edges in repaint scenario.

modified_tasks.rp_change: RP: degloss/scuff existing paint for adhesion profile (150 grit) rather than dust removal on bare substrate. Different purpose, same physical action (light sanding). Rate adjusted for existing paint hardness.
Absorbed into degloss task. NC light sand was for scuffing factory primer; RP degloss covers the same mechanical action on existing paint. Not a separate task.
RP: assess existing caulk and replace failed sections only (15-30% typical). Not full re-caulk of all joints like NC.
RP: state-driven primer (adhesion or stain-block) instead of bare-substrate primer. Conditional on substrate state — no primer for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT.
Eliminated — RP restricts to brush_roll only. Spray not offered for closet shelving RP.
Eliminated — RP restricts to QT2-QT3. Interstage sanding is QT4/QT5 only per NC applies_when.

direct_transfer_tasks.notes: Identical action: drop cloth under closet opening. Same rate, same conditions.
Fill nail holes and minor defects. Same action in NC and RP.
Brush/roll finish coat(s). Same rates, same technique. Coat count per QT (QT2=1, QT3=2).
Final inspection and touch-up. Same action. QT-scaled rate transfers (QT2/QT3 range only).
ELIMINATED — spray not offered in RP closet spec.
ELIMINATED — spray_rolloff not offered in RP closet spec.

rp_new_tasks.description: Brief visual condition assessment of all shelf surfaces per closet. Scan for peeling, mildew, water stains, general paint condition. Assign substrate state. Verify closet contents removed.
rp_new_tasks.notes: Single combined assessment task — no separate adhesion/coating-ID/moisture subtasks needed for closet shelving. ~2-3 min per closet.

rp_new_tasks.description: Apply biocide solution (bleach or commercial mildewcide) to mildew-affected shelf surfaces. Scrub, rinse, allow 24 hr dry.
rp_new_tasks.notes: Per-closet task — all affected surfaces in one closet treated together. Most common RP-specific task for closet shelving.

rp_new_tasks.description: Brief post-completion walkthrough with homeowner per closet. Verify shelves are coated, no drips on floor/walls, closet ready for contents replacement.
rp_new_tasks.notes: ~1-2 min per closet. Minimal compared to door/room walkthrough.

proposed_task_summary.notes: SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (most common) activates 9 always-active tasks + TSK_CSRP_PRIME_BRUSH (only if existing sheen is high enough to warrant primer — typically NO primer for sound paint). Worst case SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE activates 11 tasks (9 always + mildew treat + stain-block prime). Total 15 unique tasks, 9-11 active per job depending on state.
